note: CRL patches (revocation-tree.md, "CRL patches"). Bytes are in hex. Each case of `usable`: reading `patch` against `previous` gives `file`, and `name` is the patch's name. Each case of `unusable` cannot be used: read against `previous`, the patch breaks a rule of the format, or, for the one with a `name`, gives a file without the SHA-256 that name gives. The previous files here are not CRLs: the format does not look at what it copies.

unusable.label: a copy that ends past the end of the previous file
a copy of length 0 that starts past the end of the previous file
a copy that starts before the previous copy ended
a copy whose start and length add up past 2^32: read as 32-bit numbers, they would wrap to 1
a write whose bytes run past the end of the patch
a write of length 2^32 - 1, past the end of the patch
a write whose length runs past the end of the patch
a copy cut short in its length
a byte other than 00 and 01 after a good instruction
a well-formed patch whose file does not have the SHA-256 of its name
